players.product: PCIe / CXL retimers and high-speed interface ICs

quarterly_data.signal: Deck (server interconnect): Parade's PCIe 4/5 re-driver and re-timer were introduced in January 2023 and its PCIe 6 re-driver in September 2025; the company says it has seen more business opportunity for PCIe 6 and PCIe 7 re-drivers as data transmission speeds keep increasing, and expects a significant number of platforms using PCIe 5 / PCIe 6 / PCIe 7 to require re-drivers and re-timers. Parade has its Ethernet 56Gbps re-driver in mass production, while its 112/224 Gbps re-drivers are under engagement with Tier-1 customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Ethernet 56Gbps re-driver in mass production; 112/224 Gbps re-drivers engaged with Tier-1 customers; PCIe 6 re-driver introduced September 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Deck (financial performance, US$ million): FY25 revenue $531 versus $506 in FY24 (+5%); operating income $87 versus $76 (+14%); diluted EPS $1.10 versus $1.01 (+9%).
quarterly_data.figure: FY25 revenue US$531 million (+5%); operating income US$87 million (+14%); diluted EPS US$1.10 (+9%)
